meaning:
ἀπο-τίθημι
[in LXX chiefly for נוּחַ hi. ;]
to put off or aside; in NT always mid.,
(a) to put of from oneself as a garment: τ. ἱμάτια, Act.7:58; metaphorically, in ethical sense, to put of, lay aside: Rom.13:12, Eph.4:22, 25, Col.3:8, Heb.12:1, Jas.1:21, 1Pe.2:1;
(b) to stow away, put: ἐν τ. φυλακῇ (MM, see word), Mat.14:3.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: For Herod had arrested John, and bound him, and put him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife.
They threw him out of the city and stoned him. The witnesses placed their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
The night is far gone, and the day is near. Let’s therefore throw off the deeds of darkness, and let’s put on the armor of light.
that you put away, as concerning your former way of life, the old man that grows corrupt after the lusts of deceit,
but now you also put them all away: anger, wrath, malice, slander, and shameful speaking out of your mouth.
Therefore let’s also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let’s run…
Therefore, putting away all filthiness and overflowing of wickedness, receive with humility the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.
